learn.title: Authentication and identity management design
objectives: Choose a hybrid sign-in method (password hash sync, pass-through authentication or federation) from business requirements
Choose between Microsoft Entra Connect Sync and Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
Design MFA, passwordless, Conditional Access and risk-based policies
Recommend the right model for partners and customers: B2B collaboration, B2B direct connect or Microsoft Entra External ID
Recommend workload identities: managed identities, app registrations and workload identity federation
concepts: Password hash sync (PHS)
A hash of the on-premises password hash is synced to Microsoft Entra ID, so the cloud checks sign-ins. Simplest option; keeps working if on-premises is down and enables leaked credential detection.
Pass-through authentication (PTA)
Lightweight on-premises agents check passwords against AD DS. On-premises account state and logon hours apply right away. Agents only make outbound connections.
Federation (AD FS)
Sign-in is handed off to an on-premises federation service. Most complex; keep it only for sign-in needs that Entra ID cannot meet natively.
Seamless SSO
Signs in domain-joined devices on the corporate network silently when you use PHS or PTA. Devices that are Entra joined or hybrid joined get SSO from the Primary Refresh Token instead.
Microsoft Entra Connect Sync
Sync engine installed on a server. Supports PHS, PTA, federation, device objects for hybrid join and the full set of writeback features. HA comes from a second server in staging mode.
Microsoft Entra Cloud Sync
Lightweight agents managed from the cloud. Supports disconnected forests, multiple active agents for HA and group provisioning to AD. No PTA and no device sync.
Authentication strength
A Conditional Access grant control that requires certain methods, for example the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA strength.
Conditional Access
An if-then policy engine (needs Entra ID P1). Signals such as user, app, location, device and risk lead to block, grant or session controls.
Microsoft Entra ID Protection
Detects user risk and sign-in risk. Risk-based Conditional Access needs Microsoft Entra ID P2.
Microsoft Entra External ID (external tenant)
CIAM for consumer and customer apps: self-service sign-up, social identity providers, branding. It replaces Azure AD B2C for new customers.
Managed identity
An Entra identity for an Azure resource with no credentials to manage. A system-assigned identity shares the resource's lifecycle. A user-assigned identity is a separate resource that can be shared.
Workload identity federation

Trusts tokens from an external OIDC issuer (GitHub Actions, Kubernetes, other clouds), so no secrets are needed. You set it up as a federated credential on an app registration or user-assigned managed identity.
comparisons: PHS: least infrastructure, resilient, leaked credential detection. PTA: on-premises policy applies immediately, needs agents. Federation: only when sign-in needs can't be met in the cloud; most to run.

Use Connect Sync for PTA, federation, hybrid-join device sync and complex sync rules. Use Cloud Sync for lightweight HA agents, disconnected forests (mergers) and group provisioning to AD. The two can coexist.
Security defaults: free, all-or-nothing baseline MFA. Conditional Access: granular, needs P1, and you can't run it at the same time as security defaults.
B2B collaboration vs direct connect vs External ID
Partners who need your apps get B2B collaboration. Teams shared channels with no guest objects use B2B direct connect. Consumers and customers get an External ID external tenant.
System-assigned: one resource, deleted with it. User-assigned: shared by many resources, can be created before them, and survives redeployment.
An app registration is the application object (global definition, home tenant). An enterprise application is the service principal (local instance in each tenant that uses the app).
traps: Cloud Sync doesn't support pass-through authentication or device sync for hybrid join; those need Connect Sync.
Leaked credential detection needs password hash sync. You can turn PHS on alongside PTA or federation.
Risk-based Conditional Access needs P2; ordinary Conditional Access needs only P1.

Microsoft Authenticator push with number matching is strong but isn't phishing-resistant. Phishing-resistant means WHfB, FIDO2 passkeys (including Authenticator passkeys) or certificate-based authentication.
B2B direct connect is only for Teams shared channels and creates no guest account in your directory.
Azure AD B2C is no longer sold to new customers. New customer identity designs use Microsoft Entra External ID.
revision: Default hybrid choice: password hash sync plus Seamless SSO, managed with Connect Sync or Cloud Sync.
For PTA HA, run at least three agents. For Connect Sync HA, add a staging-mode server. For Cloud Sync HA, run several active agents.
Use staged rollout to move from AD FS to cloud authentication group by group.
Pilot Conditional Access in report-only mode, block legacy authentication, and use authentication strengths for admins.
Partner MFA prompts are handled by inbound trust in cross-tenant access settings.
Cross-tenant synchronization automates B2B users across the tenants of one organisation.
Prefer a managed identity over secrets for Azure-hosted code. Prefer workload identity federation for GitHub Actions and AKS.
